extracted.intended_audience: humor writers, satirists, and students of Dorothy Parker/Algonquin wit
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting brief, quotable one-liners and puns in the Dorothy Parker / Algonquin Round Table tradition: truth-bearing, polite-yet-cutting, often improvised quips intended for rapid delivery and republication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit must contain truth
rubrics_metrics.description: "Wit has truth in it; wisecracking is simply calisthenics with words."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish genuine wit (insightful, truth-bearing) from empty wisecracks (mere verbal exercise). A successful Parker-style line reveals or reframes a recognizable truth about people or situations. Examples: 'Heterosexuality is not normal, it's just common.' Anti-pattern: clever phrasing with no insight or recognizably true bite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and quotability (compression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the sentence brief and quotable? Single sentences carry full essays of meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for compressed one-liners that encapsulate an observation in a single, re-usable line. Examples: 'Brevity is the soul of lingerie.' Avoid long-winded setups that dilute the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound-based wordplay (pun, alliteration, rhyme)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it use sound (pun, alliteration, rhyme)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use homophones, near-homophones, alliteration, or rhyme to produce a second meaning through sound. Technique example: 'Pun via Sound Substitution' — replace a word with a homophone to create a new reading ('You can lead a horticulture but you can't make her think.'). Be careful that the sound-play supports the truth/insight rather than existing for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level contradiction / reversal (setup + reversal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Setup + reversal in the same line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a single-line structure that sets up an expectation and immediately subverts it for comic effect. This is central to Parker-style quips. Example: transform a familiar proverb or expectation into an ironic twist. Avoid reversals that feel arbitrary or unrelated to the setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polite-yet-cutting tone (truth-telling politeness)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a surface of civility or elegant phrasing while delivering an edge of insult or hard truth. The cadence should feel socially acceptable even as it wounds. Anti-pattern: crude or mean-spirited attacks that lack the veneer of politeness and therefore lose Parker's characteristic wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rereadability / layered meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Could it be re-read and still land?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft lines with layered meanings or compressed density so that subsequent readings reveal additional cleverness. A good Parker quip rewards re-reading rather than collapsing after the first laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediacy and improvisational agility
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapid one-liners as competitive sport; ability to turn a word into a pun quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop rapid-response skill (as in the Round Table game: 'I can give you a sentence' — turn a multi-syllabic word into a pun in seconds). This evaluates performance ability and timing as much as the finished line. Practice producing quips under time pressure; anti-pattern: overworked lines that lose spontaneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of insider references and cultivated public persona
rubrics_metrics.description: Insider references and cultivation of public reputation as wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algonquin-style quips often trade on shared cultural or social knowledge; a cultivated reputation amplifies reception. Evaluate whether references land for the intended audience and whether the speaker's persona supports the line. Caution: heavy insiderism can limit broader quotability.
